title: Nepal lifts curb on Indian Rs 200, Rs 500 notes for travellers up to Rs 25,000 - India Today
description: Nepal lifts curb on Indian Rs 200, Rs 500 notes for travellers up to Rs 25,000  India Today
publisher.title: India Today
full_article:
Nepal has allowed Indian and Nepalese nationals to carry Indian currency notes of Rs 200 and Rs 500 into and out of the country, ending a restriction that had effectively limited travellers to notes of up to Rs 100 after India’s 2016 demonetisation. The revised provision keeps the existing ceiling of Rs 25,000 per person.

The Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB), in a notice reissued on Thursday, said Indian and Nepalese nationals may carry Indian currency notes of Rs 200 and Rs 500 denominations issued on or after November 9, 2016, in line with prevailing regulations. The central bank said the rules had already been notified through a notice published in the Nepal Gazette on February 11 after the required regulations were framed, and the latest notice was issued to reiterate the rules and clarify their implementation.

Clarifying the rules, NRB spokesperson Guru Prasad Paudel said on Saturday that Nepalese nationals cannot bring Indian currency into Nepal from any country other than India. Similarly, they cannot carry Indian currency from Nepal to a third country, except India. He said the revised provision would help Indian tourists visiting Nepal and Nepalese nationals involved in trade and business with India.

The notice also said Nepalese nationals and foreign visitors can bring up to USD 5,000, or its equivalent in other foreign currencies, into Nepal without making a customs declaration. Amounts above USD 5,000 must be declared to customs on arrival. Paudel said travellers may bring in Indian currency equivalent to up to USD 5,000, around Rs 4.83 lakh, without a customs declaration only if the denominations do not exceed Rs 100. He added that if the amount exceeds the USD 5,000 limit, a customs declaration is mandatory.

description: Nepal eases post-demonetisation curbs on Indian currency; allows ₹200, ₹500 notes  The Hindu
publisher.title: The Hindu
full_article:
Nepal has allowed Indian and Nepalese nationals to bring into or take out of the country Indian currency notes of ₹200 and ₹500 denominations, ending a nearly decade-long restriction under which only notes of up to ₹100 denomination were permitted following India's 2016 demonetisation.

The Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB), in a notice reissued on Thursday (July 23, 2026), said Indian and Nepalese nationals may carry Indian currency notes of ₹200 and ₹500 denominations issued on or after November 9, 2016, up to a limit of ₹25,000 per person in accordance with the prevailing regulations.

A new phase in India-Nepal relations

Though the provisions had already been notified through a notice published in the Nepal Gazette on February 11 after the necessary regulations were framed, the NRB reissued the notice to reiterate the rules and clarify their implementation.

Clarifying the new rules, NRB spokesperson Guru Prasad Paudel said on Saturday (July 26) that Nepalese nationals cannot bring Indian currency into Nepal from any country other than India. Likewise, they cannot carry Indian currency from Nepal to a third country, except India.

He said the revised provision would facilitate Indian tourists visiting Nepal and Nepalese nationals engaged in trade and business with India.

The notice also said Nepalese nationals and foreign visitors can bring up to $5,000 or its equivalent in other foreign currencies into Nepal without making a customs declaration.

Amounts exceeding $5,000 must be declared to customs upon arrival.

In case of the Indian currency, travellers may bring in an amount equivalent to up to $5,000 (approx ₹4.83 lakh) without making a customs declaration only if the denominations do not exceed ₹100, Mr. Paudel said.

However, if the amount exceeds the $5,000 limit, a customs declaration is mandatory, he added.

India demonetised ₹500 and ₹1,000 currency notes on November 8, 2016, replacing them with redesigned ₹500 notes and introducing new ₹2,000 notes, which have since been withdrawn from circulation.

Following the demonetisation, Nepal prohibited the entry and use of Indian currency notes of denominations above ₹100. While the ceiling of ₹25,000 on carrying Indian currency remained unchanged, travellers were effectively restricted to notes of ₹100 and below.

Under the revised regulations, Indian and Nepalese nationals are now permitted to carry redesigned ₹500 notes and ₹200 notes issued after November 9, 2016, subject to the existing ceiling of ₹25,000.

Indian currency notes of ₹500 and ₹1,000 denominations issued before that date will continue to remain prohibited in Nepal.

The move is expected to facilitate travel and cross-border transactions between India and Nepal, which share an open border and close people-to-people ties. India is Nepal's largest trading partner and a major source of tourists, while thousands of Nepalese citizens live, work, study and conduct business in India.

नेपाल राष्ट्र बैंक (एनआरबी) गुरुवार (23 जुलाई, 2026) क पुनः जारी सूचना मे कहलक अछि जे भारतीय आ नेपाली नागरिक ₹200 आ ₹500 मूल्यक नोट प्रचलित नियमक अनुसार 9 नवम्बर 2016 या ओकर बाद जारी कएल गेल भारतीय मुद्रा नोट ₹25,000 प्रति व्यक्तिक सीमा तक ल सकैत अछि।

भारत-नेपाल संबंध मे एकटा नव चरण

यद्यपि आवश्यक नियमावली के निर्माण के बाद नेपाल राजपत्र में प्रकाशित सूचना के माध्यम स प्रावधान के अधिसूचना भ चुकल छल, मुदा एनआरबी नियम के दोहराबय आ ओकर क्रियान्वयन के स्पष्ट करय लेल नोटिस फेर सं जारी केलक अछि.

नव नियम स्पष्ट करैत एनआरबीक प्रवक्ता गुरुप्रसाद पौडेल शनिदिन (२६ जुलाई) कहलनि जे, नेपाली नागरिक भारतक अतिरिक्त कोनो देश सँ भारतीय मुद्रा नेपाल मे नहि आनि सकैत अछि । तहिना भारत छोड़ि नेपाल सँ तेसर देश मे भारतीय मुद्रा नहि पहुँचा सकैत छथि ।

ओ कहला जे संशोधित प्रावधान स नेपाल आबय वाला भारतीय पर्यटक आ भारत स व्यापार आ व्यापार मे लागल नेपाली नागरिक कए सुविधा भेटत।

नोटिस मे इहो कहल गेल अछि जे नेपाली नागरिक आ विदेशी आगंतुक बिना सीमा शुल्क घोषणा केने ५ हजार डॉलर या ओकर समकक्ष अन्य विदेशी मुद्रा मे नेपाल आनि सकैत अछि ।

5000 डॉलर सं बेसि राशि कें आगमन पर सीमा शुल्क कें घोषणा करनाय आवश्यक छै.

श्री पौडेल कहलनि जे, भारतीय मुद्रा के मामला मे यात्री बिना कस्टम घोषणा केने 5000 डॉलर (लगभग ₹4.83 लाख) तक के राशि तबे आनि सकैत छथि जखन कि संप्रदाय ₹100 स बेसी नहि हो।

मुदा, जौं इ राशि 5000 डॉलर क सीमा स बेसी भ गेल त सीमा शुल्क घोषणा अनिवार्य अछि, ओ इहो कहलनि।

भारत न॑ ८ नवंबर २०१६ क॑ ₹५०० आरू ₹१,००० मुद्रा नोट क॑ विमुद्रित करी क॑ ओकरऽ जगह प॑ नया रूप स॑ डिजाइन करलऽ गेलऽ ₹५०० नोट आरू नया ₹2,000 नोट पेश करलकै, जेकरा बाद स॑ प्रचलन स॑ हटाय देलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

विमुद्रीकरण के बाद नेपाल ₹100 स बेसी के भारतीय मुद्रा नोट के प्रवेश आ उपयोग पर रोक लगा देलक। भारतीय मुद्रा ले जाय के ₹25,000 के सीमा जहाँ अपरिवर्तित रहलै, वहीं यात्री सिनी क॑ प्रभावी ढंग स॑ ₹100 आरू ओकरा स॑ कम के नोट प॑ सीमित करी देलऽ गेलै ।

संशोधित नियमावली के तहत भारतीय आरू नेपाली नागरिक क॑ अब॑ ९ नवंबर २०१६ के बाद जारी करलऽ गेलऽ नया रूप स॑ डिजाइन करलऽ गेलऽ ₹500 के नोट आरू ₹200 के नोट ले जाय के अनुमति छै, जेकरऽ मौजूदा सीमा ₹25,000 के अधीन छै ।

ओहि तिथि सँ पहिने जारी ₹500 आ ₹1,000 मूल्यक भारतीय मुद्रा नोट नेपाल मे निषिद्ध रहत।

ई कदम स॑ भारत आरू नेपाल के बीच यात्रा आरू सीमा पार स॑ लेनदेन म॑ सुविधा मिलै के उम्मीद छै, जेकरा म॑ खुला सीमा आरू जनता स॑ घनिष्ठ संबंध छै । भारत नेपालक सबसँ पैघ व्यापारिक भागीदार आ पर्यटकक प्रमुख स्रोत अछि, जखन कि हजारों नेपाली नागरिक भारतमे रहैत अछि, काज करैत अछि, पढ़ैत अछि आ व्यापार करैत अछि ।

Travelling To Nepal? New Rule Lets You Carry Up To Rs 25,000 In Rs 200 And Rs 500 Indian Notes

Published By : Mallika Soni

, News18.com

Last Updated: July 26, 2026, 12:48 IST

Only the redesigned Rs 500 notes issued after November 9, 2016, and Rs 200 notes are now permitted.

Nepal has long been a favorite among Indian tourists due to its proximity, shared cultural and religious ties, and incredible natural beauty. (Representational image: Canva)

If you’re planning a trip to Nepal, there’s good news. The country relaxed a nearly decade-old restriction on Indian currency, allowing travellers to carry redesigned Rs 200 and Rs 500 notes once again. The move reverses a key restriction that had been in place since India’s 2016 demonetisation and is expected to make travel and cross-border transactions much smoother.

Here’s what you need to know:

What Has Changed?

Nepal allowed Indian and Nepalese nationals to carry Indian currency notes of Rs 200 and redesigned Rs 500 denominations into and out of the country. Earlier, travellers were effectively restricted to carrying only Rs 100 notes, even though the overall limit of Rs 25,000 remained unchanged. The revised rules apply only to Rs 200 and Rs 500 notes issued on or after November 9, 2016.

How Much Indian Currency Can You Carry?

The maximum amount remains Rs 25,000 per person. This means Indian and Nepalese nationals can now carry up to Rs 25,000 in eligible Rs 200 and Rs 500 notes while travelling between the two countries.

Why Were Rs 200 And Rs 500 Notes Banned Earlier?

After India demonetised Rs 500 and Rs 1,000 notes on November 8, 2016, Nepal barred the entry and use of Indian currency notes above Rs 100. Although India later introduced redesigned Rs 500 notes and new Rs 200 notes, Nepal continued with the restriction for several years.

Can You Carry Old Rs 500 Notes?

No. Only the redesigned Rs 500 notes issued after November 9, 2016, and Rs 200 notes are now permitted. The old pre-demonetisation Rs 500 and Rs 1,000 notes remain prohibited in Nepal.

Who Benefits From New Rules?

According to Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB), the revised provision is expected to benefit indian tourists visiting Nepal, Nepalese citizens travelling to India, traders and businesses engaged in cross-border commerce. The move is expected to make everyday transactions significantly more convenient.

Are There Any Other Restrictions?

Yes. Nepal Rastra Bank clarified that Nepalese nationals cannot bring Indian currency into Nepal from any country other than India. Similarly, they cannot carry Indian currency from Nepal to a third country. Indian currency can only be transported between India and Nepal.

What Are Customs Rules?

The NRB has also reiterated its foreign exchange regulations. Travellers can bring up to USD 5,000, or its equivalent in foreign currency, into Nepal without filing a customs declaration. However, if the amount exceeds USD 5,000, a customs declaration is mandatory upon arrival. The central bank also clarified that Indian currency equivalent to up to USD 5,000 can be brought into Nepal without a declaration only if it is in Rs 100 or lower denominations.

नव नियम स केकरा फायदा होइत छैक ?

नेपाल राष्ट्र बैंक (एनआरबी) के अनुसार संशोधित प्रावधान स नेपाल आबय वाला भारतीय पर्यटक, भारत आबय वाला नेपाली नागरिक, सीमा पार वाणिज्य मे लागल व्यापारी आ व्यवसायी के लाभ पहुंचेबाक उम्मीद अछि। उम्मीद अछि जे एहि कदम स रोजमर्रा क लेनदेन काफी सुविधाजनक भ जाएत।

KATHMANDU, JULY 26

Police have recovered 140 kilograms of marijuana hidden inside an orchard in Parsa district during a targeted search operation based on a tip-off, officials said.

According to District Police Office, Parsa, a joint team from the Parsa Police Office and the Armed Police Force's BOP Mirjapur conducted a search at an orchard in Mirjapur, of Chhipaharmai Rural Municipality-2, at around 11:30 pm on July 25.

During the search, police found 13 packages containing 140 kg of marijuana concealed inside a pile of grass in the orchard. The contraband was seized and further investigation has been launched.

title: 1.2 million tourists entered Nepal in one year, 25 percent Indian - OnlineKhabar English News
description: 1.2 million tourists entered Nepal in one year, 25 percent Indian  OnlineKhabar English News
publisher.title: OnlineKhabar English News
full_article:
Tourists trekking in Nepal along the Annapurna circuit. Photo: Anuska Pradhan

Kathmandu, July 26

In fiscal year 2025/26, 1,209,357 foreign tourists entered Nepal. According to the Nepal Tourism Board, the largest number, 311,531, came from India, while 111,325 tourists came from the United States and 109,892 from China.

According to international tourist arrival data released by the Nepal Tourism Board, India has become Nepal’s largest source market, accounting for about 25.76 percent of total arrivals. After India, the United States (111,325) is the second-largest source market, and China (109,892) is the third.

They were followed by 58,163 tourists from Bangladesh, 56,649 from the United Kingdom, 53,195 from Australia, 43,211 from Sri Lanka, 36,289 from Bhutan, 30,737 from Myanmar, 29,296 from Germany, 27,201 from Thailand, 25,762 from Japan, and 25,640 from Malaysia.

In the last fiscal year 2025/26, the highest number of foreign tourists, 124,829, arrived in mid-October to mid-November 2025. This was followed by 119,390 in mid-March to mid-April 2026, 114,152 in mid-February to mid-March 2026, and 111,780 in mid-September to mid-October 2025, according to the data.

The Nepal Tourism Board said it has intensified promotional programs in its closest source markets, India and China. In fiscal year 2025/26, more than 12 promotional events were held in various Indian cities including Pune, Hyderabad, Chennai, Mumbai, and New Delhi. In total, more than 40 tourism promotional events for Nepal were held in international markets.

Similarly, in the last three months of fiscal year 2025/26, various cross-border tourism marts and fairs were held from Jhapa in the east to Kanchanpur in the west, to safeguard investment in tourism infrastructure in Nepal’s Tarai region bordering India. The Board’s analysis shows this led to a notable rise in the number of tourists entering Nepal through the border areas.

Nepal Tourism Board Acting Chief Executive Hikmat Singh Airee said Nepal’s tourism has grown positively due to international market promotion, expanded air access, and cooperation with the private sector.

He said, “Tourist arrivals in fiscal year 2025/26 clearly indicate that Nepal’s tourism industry is moving from recovery toward sustainable growth. Alongside our major source markets, we will continue making targeted promotion in new, promising markets more effective, in our ongoing effort to establish Nepal as an attractive year-round destination.”

Acting Chief Executive Airee pointed out that although China has enormous potential for tourist arrivals, sales missions targeting that market need to be made more effective to expand business-to-business (B2B) contacts.

He said, “To strengthen our presence further in new, high-potential source markets such as the US, Australia and Bangladesh, alongside China, we need to run regular international sales missions. To make tourism promotion more results-oriented, the Nepal Tourism Board is moving to expand such programs immediately in cooperation with the private sector through the fiscal year 2026/27 budget.”

Noting that the Government of Nepal has declared this year the Wellness Tourism Year 2027, Acting Chief Executive Airee said tourist arrival numbers are expected to rise further in the current fiscal year. The Nepal Tourism Board said it will work in the coming days to attract high-spending tourists, increase length of stay, and further strengthen Nepal’s tourism promotion in both traditional and new international markets.

काठमांडू, २६ जुलाई

वित्तीय वर्ष 2025/26 मे 1,209,357 विदेशी पर्यटक नेपाल मे प्रवेश केलक। नेपाल पर्यटन बोर्डके अनुसार सबसँ बेसी संख्या ३११,५३१ भारतसँ आयल छल, जखन कि १,११,३२५ पर्यटक अमेरिकासँ आ १०९,८९२ चीनसँ आयल छल ।

नेपाल पर्यटन बोर्ड द्वारा जारी अंतर्राष्ट्रीय पर्यटक आगमन के आंकड़ा के अनुसार भारत नेपाल के सबस पैघ स्रोत बाजार बनि गेल अछि, जे कुल आगमन के लगभग 25.76 प्रतिशत अछि. भारत के बाद अमेरिका (111,325) दोसरऽ सबसें बड़ऽ स्रोत बाजार छै, आरू चीन (१०९,८९२) तेसरऽ स्थान प॑ छै ।

हुनकऽ बाद बांग्लादेश स॑ ५८,१६३, यूनाइटेड किंगडम स॑ ५६,६४९, ऑस्ट्रेलिया स॑ ५३,१९५, श्रीलंका स॑ ४३,२११, भूटान स॑ ३६,२८९, म्यांमार स॑ ३०,७३७, जर्मनी स॑ २९,२९६, थाईलैंड स॑ २७,२०१, जापान स॑ २५,७६२ आरू जापान स॑ २५,६४० पर्यटक आबी गेलै मलेशिया।

पिछला वित्तीय वर्ष 2025/26 मे अक्टूबर के मध्य सं नवंबर 2025 के मध्य तक सबस बेसी विदेशी पर्यटक 124,829 आयल छल.एकर बाद मार्च के मध्य सं अप्रैल 2026 के मध्य तक 119,390, फरवरी के मध्य सं मार्च के मध्य मे 114,152 २०२६, आरू सितम्बर के मध्य स॑ अक्टूबर २०२५ के मध्य तलक १११,७८०, आंकड़ऽ के अनुसार ।

नेपाल पर्यटन बोर्ड अपन निकटतम स्रोत बाजार भारत आ चीन मे प्रचार कार्यक्रम तेज केने बतौलक अछि । वित्तीय वर्ष 2025/26 म॑ पुणे, हैदराबाद, चेन्नई, मुंबई, आरू नई दिल्ली सहित भारत केरऽ विभिन्न शहरऽ म॑ १२ स॑ भी अधिक प्रचार कार्यक्रम आयोजित करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै । कुल मिला कए नेपाल लेल 40 स बेसी पर्यटन प्रचारक आयोजन अंतरराष्ट्रीय बाजार मे भेल।

तहिना वित्तीय वर्ष 2025/26 के अंतिम तीन महीना में भारत के सीमा स सटल नेपाल के तराई क्षेत्र में पर्यटन बुनियादी ढांचा में निवेश के सुरक्षा के लेल पूर्व में झापा स पश्चिम में कंचनपुर तक विभिन्न सीमा पार पर्यटन मार्ट आ मेला के आयोजन कायल गेल। बोर्ड केरऽ विश्लेषण स॑ पता चलै छै कि एकरा स॑ सीमावर्ती क्षेत्र स॑ नेपाल म॑ प्रवेश करै वाला पर्यटकऽ के संख्या म॑ उल्लेखनीय वृद्धि होय गेलै ।

नेपाल पर्यटन बोर्ड केरऽ कार्यवाहक मुख्य कार्यकारी हिकमत सिंह ऐरी न॑ कहलकै कि अंतरराष्ट्रीय बाजार केरऽ प्रचार, हवाई पहुँच केरऽ विस्तार, आरू निजी क्षेत्र के साथ सहयोग के कारण नेपाल केरऽ पर्यटन सकारात्मक रूप स॑ बढ़ी गेलऽ छै ।

ओ कहलनि जे, “वित्तीय वर्ष 2025/26 मे पर्यटकक आगमन स्पष्ट रूप सँ संकेत करैत अछि जे नेपालक पर्यटन उद्योग रिकवरी सँ टिकाऊ विकास दिस बढ़ि रहल अछि।अपन प्रमुख स्रोत बाजारक संग-संग हम सब नव, आशाजनक बाजार मे लक्षित प्रचार केँ बेसी प्रभावी बनबैत रहब, नेपाल केँ साल भरि आकर्षक गंतव्यक रूप मे स्थापित करबाक अपन जारी प्रयास मे।”

कार्यवाहक मुख्य कार्यकारी ऐरी न॑ ई बात के ओर इशारा करलकै कि चीन म॑ भले ही पर्यटकऽ के आगमन केरऽ अपार संभावना छै, लेकिन वू बाजार क॑ लक्षित करी क॑ बिक्री मिशन क॑ बिजनेस-टू-बिजनेस (बी टू बी) संपर्क क॑ बढ़ाबै लेली अधिक प्रभावी बनाबै के जरूरत छै ।

हुनी कहलकै, “चीन के साथ-साथ अमेरिका, ऑस्ट्रेलिया आरू बांग्लादेश जैसनौ नया, उच्च संभावना वाला स्रोत बाजार मँ अपनौ उपस्थिति क आरू मजबूत करै लेली हमरा सिनी क नियमित अंतरराष्ट्रीय बिक्री मिशन चलाबै के जरूरत छै । पर्यटन प्रचार क अधिक परिणाम उन्मुख बनाबै लेली नेपाल पर्यटन बोर्ड वित्तीय वर्ष २०२६/२७ के बजट के माध्यम स॑ निजी क्षेत्र के सहयोग स॑ ऐसनऽ कार्यक्रम के तुरंत विस्तार करै लेली आगू बढ़ी रहलऽ छै ।”

नेपाल सरकार एहि वर्ष कल्याण पर्यटन वर्ष २०२७ घोषित कएने कार्यवाहक मुख्य कार्यकारी ऐरी कहलनि जे, चालू वित्तीय वर्ष मे पर्यटकक आगमनक संख्या मे आओर बढ़ोतरी हेबाक उम्मीद अछि। नेपाल पर्यटन बोर्ड आगामी दिन मे बेसी खर्च करय वाला पर्यटक के आकर्षित करय, प्रवास के अवधि बढ़ाबय, आ पारंपरिक आ नव अंतर्राष्ट्रीय दुनु बाजार मे नेपाल के पर्यटन प्रचार के आओर मजबूत करय के काज करत से कहलक अछि.
